title: An AI Breakthrough Has Made Decades of Computer Science Research ‘Irrelevant’
gist: OpenAI and Anthropic both claimed this week to have disproved the 27-year-old exponential time hypothesis (ETH), a foundation of complexity theory, potentially invalidating large swaths of research, including around 50 papers by one UC Santa Barbara professor. The proofs remain unverified, and researchers describe both excitement and psychological strain as AI results repeatedly upend fields, alongside concerns about volume, slop and IPO-driven rollouts.

insights.claim: Both OpenAI and Anthropic claimed this week to have disproved the exponential time hypothesis, the 27-year-old premise that the effort to solve certain problems grows exponentially with problem size.
insights.speaker: Isabella Ward
insights.so_what: Frontier labs are now competing on landmark mathematical results, not just benchmarks.
insights.quote: Both OpenAI and Anthropic claimed this week to have disproved the exponential time hypothesis (ETH).

insights.claim: The AI-produced proofs have been published on GitHub in natural language and machine-checkable Lean but have not yet been independently verified.
insights.speaker: Isabella Ward
insights.so_what: Formal verification in Lean could accelerate acceptance, but the claim is still provisional.

insights.claim: If confirmed, the result would make around 50 of Daniel Lokshtanov's published papers pointless or in need of revisiting.
insights.speaker: Daniel Lokshtanov
insights.so_what: AI results can obsolete entire research portfolios overnight.
insights.quote: It’s just a giant bomb dropped into the middle of the field
insights.locator: UC Santa Barbara professor Daniel Lokshtanov

insights.claim: Peter Jonsson expects many talks at the IEEE Symposium on Foundations of Computer Science to begin by admitting ETH is false and half their paper does not work.
insights.speaker: Peter Jonsson
entities: IEEE Symposium on Foundations of Computer Science
insights.so_what: Academic conference cycles are lagging AI-driven discovery.
insights.quote: People will start the talks: ‘ETH is false, half of my paper does not work,’

insights.claim: A Copenhagen algorithms researcher calls the result fantastic, likening it to floodlights illuminating an entire subfield that can now be explored, in contrast to the ennui among mathematicians facing other AI proofs.
insights.speaker: Thore Husfeldt
insights.so_what: AI breakthroughs can open new research frontiers rather than only displacing researchers.
insights.quote: It's like somebody just illuminated an entire subfield in floodlights of knowledge

insights.claim: Researchers plan to revisit problems previously abandoned under the assumption that ETH was true.
insights.speaker: Victor Lagerkvist
insights.so_what: Second-order wave of new algorithmic results likely to follow.

insights.claim: While the ETH result does not directly affect cryptography, it should scare some cryptosystem designers because web security rests on assumptions that certain problems take impractically long to solve.
insights.speaker: Daniel Lokshtanov
insights.so_what: Hardness assumptions underpinning digital infrastructure and crypto assets face increased AI-driven scrutiny.
insights.quote: it should definitely scare some cryptosystem designers
insights.locator: OpenAI’s finding could also have impacts

insights.claim: Continued human and AI-assisted theoretical work matters because much modern digital infrastructure is built on assumptions about computation.
insights.speaker: Thore Husfeldt
insights.so_what: Validating computational assumptions is a security-relevant research priority.
insights.quote: lots of modern digital infrastructure is built on assumptions about computation

insights.claim: AI results announced every week or two have been annihilating ongoing research projects, and one department has considered hiring an occupational psychologist because some researchers are depressed.
insights.speaker: Thore Husfeldt
insights.so_what: AI's acceleration of science carries labor and morale costs in academia.
insights.quote: every week, or every second week, the results announced by AI just annihilate the ongoing research projects of many people
insights.locator: The last few months have been really tough

insights.claim: Researchers are overwhelmed by AI-generated content including slop-level papers, and reading math is a large cognitive investment they cannot spend on unvetted submissions.
insights.speaker: Thore Husfeldt
insights.so_what: Verification capacity, not generation, is becoming the bottleneck in AI-era science.
insights.quote: Reading math is a very big investment of cognitive time

insights.claim: Earlier this month OpenAI dumped 722 manuscripts on 400 problems on GitHub, some containing errors, which some mathematicians saw as a hasty rollout designed to boost its planned IPO.
insights.speaker: Isabella Ward
insights.so_what: Research announcements may be timed to support OpenAI's IPO narrative; investors should discount volume over verified quality.
insights.quote: reflecting what some mathematicians saw as a hasty rollout designed to juice the company’s planned initial public offering
insights.locator: OpenAI has directly contributed to this

insights.claim: OpenAI is funding a conference and recruiting the hypothesis's original proposers and an MIT academic to rally researchers to unpack the proofs; its 60-odd-page ETH paper is reportedly better written than past releases.
insights.speaker: Isabella Ward
insights.so_what: Labs are investing in academic validation to legitimize AI-generated results.
